finding: F-SI29 qualifies the dynamic B1.10 top-boundary component, but the current soil-water top-boundary interface cannot transport whether a provider selected a flux or prescribed-head regime. HeadCalc therefore cannot consume all F-SI29-qualified regimes through the typed solver-service path.

solver_contract.missing_output: explicit selected top-boundary regime / head-vs-flux discriminator

headcalc.behavior: boundtop_state_bridge() sets state%ftoph=.false. unconditionally whenever provider_top_active, then marks provider runoff resolved
headcalc.consequence: An explicit provider can currently drive only the flux residual branch even when F-SI29 selected atmospheric-head or ponded-head physics.

architectural_consequence: Proceeding in F-KT15 now would silently replace qualified dynamic head/flux switching with a flux-only top boundary and violate physics-vs-policy separation, SWAP-physics reuse and the frozen F-KT15 fail-closed contract.

required_predecessor.scope: Extend the common top-boundary provider result contract with an explicit regime discriminator and make HeadCalc consume it without changing F-SI29 physics; qualify flux, atmospheric-head and ponded-head residual routing plus linear-runoff metadata, fallback and O0/O2 identity.
must_not: move task-3 bookkeeping into the solver

fkt15_rule_until_predecessor_qualified: Fail closed. Keep SoilWater(2) on unchanged direct HeadCalc production routing and publish no solver-service sensitivity from that route.
